introduction: Connecticut’s earned income tax credit is a refundable state tax credit for eligible workers. It is claimed with the state income-tax return.
description: Connecticut’s earned income tax credit is a refundable state tax credit for eligible workers. It is claimed with the state income-tax return.

sections.who: You must qualify for federal EITC and satisfy Connecticut rules, including full-year residency. Earned income, filing status, tax identification and any qualifying-child rules affect eligibility.
sections.get: The credit can reduce state income tax or contribute to a refund. Use the calculation and limits for the filing year.
sections.docs:
• Federal return, wage statements and self-employment income and expense records.
  • Social Security numbers required for eligible filers and children.
  • Full-year residency and qualifying-child records, where applicable.
sections.apply:
1. Confirm federal and state eligibility

    Review the DRS EITC page and the correct year’s instructions.

  2. Complete Schedule CT-EITC

    Use information from the federal return and retain any calculation worksheets.

  3. File the Connecticut return

    Include the required schedule. If needed, look for qualified free tax-preparation help before the filing deadline.
sections.after: DRS may request supporting records. Respond to the actual notice and retain the federal and state returns together.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Connecticut EITC eligibility and schedule guidance. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Do I need a qualifying child?
